newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's says enters India beer market.
newsitem.headline: Foster's says enters India beer market.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Thursday it had become the first foreign brewer to establish operations in India with a A$18 million investment in a 35 million litre brewery near Mumbai.
"We believe Foster's India will be making profits for its shareholders within four years of our commencement date," chief executive Ted Kunkel said in a statement.
Foster's said work had already begun on the brewery, of which it would own 51 percent and India's Kothari Industrial Corp 24 percent. The remaining 25 percent would be held by other Indian partners.
The brewery, which will reach 10 million litres later this year, was being built in Aurangabad, a satellite city servicing Mumbai, the world's third largest city.
Foster's said it would brew its lager for India's premium market, supplemented by a new, quality brand for the "everyday" market.
Both markets, currently dominated by Indian brands, were seen underpinned by demand from a growing Indian middle class.
"It is still early days for the Indian beer market, but all the signs are extremely promising," Kunkel said.
"Foster's will be in a perfect position to capitalise on an inevitable growth in beer consumption, as a vast middle class emerges in India."
Indian beer consumption was only a third of Australian's annual consumption of about 1.7 billion litres but demand was increasing at over 15 percent a year and margins were solid, Foster's said.
It said the lager-orientated Indian market favoured beer as a healthier alternative to traditional alcoholic spirits.
The India brewery was the next significant step in Foster's Asian strategy which saw it enter China four years ago, Foster's said.
"India is a logical next step for Foster's. A brewery of this size and location is a sensible investment for the future," Kunkel said.
